Subject Anonymous letter to the Police Department regarding the "I Lin
Dramatic Club".
Made by C.D.I. Sin Tse-liang Forwarded by C. [Signature]

With reference to the attached anonymous letter
containing an allegation against the "I Lin Dramatic
Club", I beg to report that this organization which is
known to the Municipal Police as the Shanghai Nyi Ling
Dramatic Society (藝林劇社), first came into
existence at the beginning of 1938 with the object of
studying drama and promoting amusements and an
application for registration was subsequently made by
its promoters to the Special Branch, Shanghai Municipal
Police but retained, pending consideration.

During the period, a watch was kept on the
activities of this Society and it was seen that in
1938, members of the Society staged only two shows:
the first time at the so-called "Little Theatre", now
defunct, at 730 Foochow Road, for six days beginning
from February 5, 1938, and the second time in
conjunction with other dramatic societies at the
so-called Shanghai Sunday Theatre, now defunct, located
in the Strand Theatre, Ningpo Road, for one day only.
The plays on both occasions were censored by S. 3
Special Branch and found to contain nothing objectionable.

Owing to lack of sufficient funds, this Society
was practically inactive except for staging the two
shows mentioned above.

On January 30, 1939, the principal promoters of
this Society decided to resuscitate the activities of
the Society and submitted a further application to the

事由：关于“艺林剧社”致警务处的匿名信。
由 刑事侦缉督察 辛子良（Sin Tse-liang）呈报 经手人 C. [签名]

兹就所附指控“艺林剧社”的匿名信一事，谨报告如下：该组织为工部局警务处所熟知的上海艺林剧社（Shanghai Nyi Ling Dramatic Society，藝林劇社），于1938年初成立，旨在研究戏剧及推广娱乐活动。其发起人随后向上海公共租界工部局警务处特科提交了注册申请，但该申请暂被保留，以待审议。

在此期间，警方对该社的活动进行了监视，发现该社成员在1938年仅演出了两场剧目：第一场是在福州路730号所谓的“小剧场”（Little Theatre，现已停业），自1938年2月5日起为期六天；第二场是与其他剧社联合，在宁波路斯特兰德大戏院（Strand Theatre）内所谓的“上海星期剧场”（Shanghai Sunday Theatre，现已停业）演出，仅有一天。这两次演出的剧本均经由特科第三股（S. 3 Special Branch）审查，未发现任何违禁内容。

由于缺乏足够资金，除上述两次演出外，该社实际上处于不活跃状态。

此后，该社每逢周日上午在卡尔登大戏院（Carlton Theatre）进行演出。演出剧目的剧情梗概事先均经由特科第三股审查。

该社目前由一个七人委员会管理，成员均为年轻男性，身份为学生或店员（参见1939年2月7日特科报告）。目前拥有男女青年会员37名，会员名单附于本报告之后并附有译文。虽然无法确切说明他们在1937年中日敌对行动爆发后是否参与了救国运动，但本局档案中并无任何对其不利的记录。总体而言，该社的运作方式实际上与不时在租界各地进行演出的众多其他业余剧社相同。

该社两位主要发起人江寅先生（Mr. Kiang Ying）和姜衍先生（Mr. Chiang Yeng）在1939年3月15日的面谈中被问及是否与其他组织或党派发生过冲突。他们回答说，除了大约一个月前因某些财务问题与该社一名前同事发生私人争吵（该纠纷已友好解决）外，他们与社会大众相安无事。

对匿名信信封的检查显示，该信于1939年3月3日下午3时在福州路与江西路拐角处的开发大楼（Development Building）第24支邮局投寄。

就涉案信件的笔迹和措辞咨询了刑侦科笔迹专家、文书助理梅约（Mei Yoh）先生。

虽然刑侦科档案中没有任何记录可以指向写信人的身份，但梅先生认为，该笔迹并非自然书写，而是故意伪装的。

署名“Pi Mi Tang Pu”意为“秘密党徒”。工部局警务处从未听说过该党派，且为查明其身份所作的一切努力均未成功。

信上盖有两个不同印章的三个印迹。其中一个盖有两处印迹的印章刻有“警告”二字；这显然是一个外行在一块橡胶上刻制的。该印章上还标有数字583，这可能意味着或意在传达此信是该社团档案中的第583封信，即此前已发出了582封类似性质的信件。

In addition Wong Chueh's personal chop is of quite

另一枚较小的印章刻有“王珏”（Wong Chueh）字样，这与一直协助艺林社演出的一名演员的名字相符。王珏，别名王培宝（Wong Bei Pao），上海人，25岁，无固定职业，与其亲戚同住静安寺路1280号。他靠在康纳路（Connaught Road，今淮海中路）1109号新华影业公司（Nyi Hwa Studio，O.O.L.）担任业余演员谋生。他未曾因任何政治活动引起警方注意。

据该剧社发起人姜衍先生（Mr. Chiang Yeng）称，王珏与他及剧组其他成员关系十分友好，没有理由怀疑王珏是负责对艺林剧社提出上述指控的人。此外，王珏的个人印章与匿名信中使用的印章外观截然不同。

值得注意的是，艺林剧社已被迫停止从3月19日开始在卡尔登大戏院的周日

Translation of anonymous letter.

____ March ____, 1939.

To
Police Department,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Sirs,

We beg to inform you that dialogue play
has been staged in the Lyceum Theatre in the
International Settlement by the "I Jin Dramatic
Club" at 10 a.m. on Sundays. The background of
that organization is too obvious. It is there-
fore requested that inquiries be made and
action taken by the police lest we should re-
sort to something untoward, detrimental to the
interests of peace and order.

(Signed): "Pi Ti Tang Tu".

S.K. Ho:
No. 134.

警务处。

敬启者：

谨告知阁下，“艺进剧社”（I Jin Dramatic Club）于周日上午10时在公共租界兰心大戏院（Lyceum Theatre）上演话剧。该组织的背景过于明显。因此，恳请警方进行调查并采取行动，以免我们采取某种不利之举，损害和平秩序之利益。

署名：“Pi Ti Tang Tu”（秘密党徒）。

第 134 号。

In accordance with the instructions of D.C. (Special

Police Headquarters on the afternoon of February 14, 1938,

registration would be retained meantime and would be given
reconsideration after a suitable period. Mr. Kiang was
further advised that during that period, programmes of any
plays which the society intended staging in the Settlement
would have to be submitted to the Special Branch for scrutiny
one week in advance. Mr. Kiang promised to comply with these
instructions.

REPORT
File No. 5350
Date February 14 1938.

Subject The Shanghai Nyi Ling Dramatic Society 上海藝林劇社 - application
for registration.
Made by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by C. Crawford. D. I.

Forwarded herewith is an application for registration submitted to the Special Branch for examination and approval by the Shanghai Nyi Ling Dramatic Society, Lane 116, House 7 Wuting Road. (Gordon Road District).

This Society came into existence on January 1, 1938 with offices at the above address and No. 700 Avenue Joffre. The object of the society is to make money by staging plays, and it is actually a professional dramatic group on a small scale.

This Society claims to have 26 members, the majority being former actors or students. The names of the chief promoters are as follows:-

Kiang Zung Yue (江潤宇), former student,
residing 21/310 Rue Ratard;

Pan Lee Sen (潘聯森), Bank clerk,
residing 5/1050 Sinza Road;

Kiang Yeng (姜衍), actor,
residing 1/316 Yates Road;

Sung Tuh Kong (孫德康), former student,
residing 126 Sze Hou Lee, Hardon Road.

According to the records of this office, these names have not come to the notice of the Special Branch in connection with any activities.

Between February 5th and 10th, the Shanghai Nyi Ling Dramatic Society staged two plays entitled "Storm" and "Wu Kuei Jao" (both censored and passed by S.3) at the Shanghai Recitation Hall, 730 Foochow Road. The venture was a failure and the society sustained a loss of about
